skill.name: anyviz
skill.description: Guide chart selection, consistent styling, and visualization code generation for web, Python, and R projects.
skill.summary: Create coordinated charts using 34 templates, four themes, and seven visualization library adapters.
skill.author: tseringyuu

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives involving Markdown, JavaScript strings, CSS grids, chart keys, and GeoJSON data. Confirmed risks concern immediate remote installer execution, unverified main-branch archives, and CDN scripts without integrity checks. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: README.md and README.en.md recommend executing mutable remote scripts immediately.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell and irm-to-iex examples with download, review, and verification steps using immutable release references and published signatures or digests.

remediation.issue: install.sh and install.ps1 install main-branch archives without verifying their contents.
remediation.suggestion: Pin archives to an immutable commit or release. Verify a trusted digest or signature before extraction and copying agent instructions.

remediation.issue: Four example dashboards load ECharts from jsDelivr without Subresource Integrity.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed ECharts file locally or add a verified integrity hash and crossorigin attribute to each external script tag.

content.value_statement: Charts often use unsuitable formats and inconsistent styling. Anyviz guides AI assistants through chart selection, shared themes, library adaptation, and accessibility checks.
actual_capabilities: Select charts from data structure and analytical intent using 34 statistical, geographic, network, and 3D templates.
Apply modern, analytics, dashboard, or academic themes with explicit colors, typography, spacing, and legend rules.
Guide code generation for D3.js, ECharts, Mapbox, Three.js, Matplotlib, Plotly, and ggplot2.
Coordinate entity colors, number formats, chart semantics, and interactions across multiple visualizations.
Provide accessibility guidance for contrast, redundant encodings, keyboard access, reduced motion, and alternative text.
Check supplied chart configurations with an optional Python validator for selected styling and cross-chart consistency rules.
limitations: This is a specification and workflow library, not a standalone rendering engine or hosted analytics service.
Generated visualizations require the selected libraries, suitable data, and testing in the target environment.
Example dashboards use simulated data and load ECharts from an external CDN.
The validator checks selected configuration values against hardcoded defaults; it does not verify rendered accessibility or every theme override.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use anyviz?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use its workflow and reference files as context. Integration depends on the tool configuration.

faq.question: Which visualization libraries are covered?
faq.answer: The adapters cover D3.js, ECharts, Mapbox, Three.js, Matplotlib, Plotly, and ggplot2.

faq.question: Does anyviz render charts by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides specifications, templates, examples, and guidance for generating code that uses a separate visualization library.

faq.question: Can I customize colors and themes?
faq.answer: Yes. Explicit user settings override the selected theme and defaults. Apply overrides consistently across every related chart.

faq.question: Does the validator guarantee accessibility?
faq.answer: No. It checks selected configuration rules. Contrast, keyboard behavior, label overlap, and alternative text still require separate verification.

faq.question: What should I review before installation?
faq.answer: Review installer scripts and choose an immutable source revision. The documented commands execute remote scripts, and installers update multiple detected agent directories.
